mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper supports a structure-activity rationale that amphipathicity, hydrophobic moment, and net positive charge influence antimicrobial activity of the designed alpha-helical peptides; it does not provide a direct membrane-disruption assay for K11.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: K11 and related CP-P/S16 derivative peptides

supports: hydrophobic moment, net charge, helicity, MIC/MHC/TI comparisons, and discussion of amphipathicity/net charge

mechanism_claims.limitations: No direct pore formation, membrane permeabilization, lipid binding, or in vivo mechanism assay is reported for K11 in local material.

curation_summary: Worker-6 preserved mechanism as indirect structure-activity evidence only; no direct mechanism class was promoted.
